findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be set up in fish fry station. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer bucket was prepared and tested at 100 ppm CL. Ensure a sanitizer solution is prepared during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: During the inspection, the bleach sanitizer spray at the main bar area was tested and recorded at a concentration over 200ppm. This bleach sanitizer spray bottle was pulled from service and had water added to reduce the concentration to 200ppm.Ensure test strips are used during each service to ensure the sanitizer concentration meets the proper concentration. 
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The chemical sanitizer spray bottle in the fry area was tested and recorded at 0ppm. Bleach was added to this spray bottle and brought into compliance at 100ppm. The spray bottle should be tested at regular intervals to ensure the sanitizer concentration is sufficeint for sanitizing surfaces.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: Workers were observed engaging in food preparation activities without first washing their hands. Workers were instructed to remove their gloves, wash their hands in the designated hand sink and then they may equip gloves. Ensure that workers properly wasn’t heir hands between tasks and before engaging in food service activities.
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: The sink basins in the frying building were observed to be utilized for purposes besides hand washing. With 2 sink basins, during food preparation and service, one of the sink basins need to be designated as an official hand sink in order for the workers to have access to a hand sink. Ensure a sink basin is designated with appropriate signage, soap, and disposable paper towels.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The ice scoop holder and the can opener were observed soiled at the start of the inspection. Each items was removed form service and placed into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. Ensure that food contact surfaces remain clean to sight and touch. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11: The baffle of the ice machine is observed to have an accumulation of mold/soil residues along the metal fold and the edges of the baffle. Ensure this surface is properly cleaned and sanitized and then cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean.
4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: The fry building is observed to have an accumulation of rodent droppings along the interior walls of the back room, galley room, and main room. Fidelis is the facility PCO and should be contacted and made aware of the observations and discuss plans for eradication. A follow-up is being issued for Monday, November 7th, 2022 to observe the eradication and prevention process.
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: At the start of the inspection, the tongs to utilized to remove fish from the fryers were observed stored with the contact surface in contact with a very soiled metal piece. The tongs were removed from this location and placed properly on the food basins. Ensure utensils intended for food contact are stored in a manner that prevents contamination.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.comment:
5-403.11: It was confirmed in the fry building that the mop water is dumped outside and not through a proper disposal system. This practice should stop and the mop water should be disposed of utilizing the public sewer. Ensure workers are educated and the effort is established to properly dispose of waste water.
5-403.11: SEWAGE shall be disposed through an APPROVED facility that is: (A) A public SEWAGE treatment plant (B) An individual SEWAGE disposal system that is sized, constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: Facility is observed to have an accumulation of rodent droppings, dead insects, and other various debris/soils in the fry room back room, galley room, and main room. Ensure that equipment is pulled away from walls and that the premise is cleaned with the removal of the droppings, insects, and various debris/soils.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.citation_text:
2-401.11 Personal beverages in plastic cups were observed on shelving in dry storage area by single service articles and other items used during food service. Provide a designated area for personal drink storage separate from storage and prep areas. 
Food employees may drink from a closed beverage container if the container is handled to prevent contamination of: the employee’s hands; the container; and exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single-service and single-use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.
--Worker was observed eating while preparing food in the main kitchen. Worker was advised to cease eating in the same area where he is preparing food for customers. Taste testing needs to be done in a manner that doesn't pose a risk of potential cross contamination.
Employees shall eat only in designated areas where the contamination of exposed food; clean equipment, utensils, and linens; unwrapped single service and single use articles; or other items needing protection cannot result.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12 Workers in the main kitchen and the cook shack were observed washing hands without proper technique. Process took less than 20 seconds, and paper towels were not used as a barrier to shut off the faucet. Poster showing proper technique is posted in both locations. PIC was advised to reiterate proper handwashing process with all workers. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

2-301.14 While discussing handwashing with one worker, another person stated he washed his hands in the restroom prior to putting on gloves. Worker was advised that handwashing upon entering the kitchen and prior to putting on gloves needs to occur in addition to washing hands in the restroom. Worker washed hands and put on a new pair of gloves. 
--Worker entered the cook shack and did not wash hands prior to putting on gloves to work with food. Handwashing upon entering the cook shack and prior to glove use were discussed. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed upon entering the work area, prior to putting on gloves/between glove changes, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.15 Worker dipped hands in detergent solution at the 3 part sink for handwashing. Worker was advised on proper handwashing at the designated handsink. Worker used the handsink to wash his hands upon request of inspector. 
Food employees shall clean their hands in a handwashing sink or approved automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for food prep, or warewashing, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11 Both basins at two part sink in the cook shack had various items in them. The handwashing signage was posted in the middle of the two basins. The left basin was designated for handwashing during inspection, and all items moved to the right basin. Ensure the left basin is maintained clean and properly stocked for handwashing only. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted in the women's restroom. Handwashing sign was provided. 
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Carbon copy paper used for taking orders was placed directly on top of cooked fish in area where orders were being assembled. Papers were removed and placed on the counter. PIC advised workers on placing papers on the counter and not in direct contact with food. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code and single service and single use articles.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114 Bleach solution setup for ware washing was observed at 50-100ppm. Concentration required for product in use is 150-200ppm. Solution was remade at 150-200ppm. 
A chlorine solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain bleach solutions at 150-200ppm, and use test strips to verify concentration.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold accumulation was observed on the lower ledge of the baffle and the ceiling behind the baffle in the ice machine. Cleaning frequency was discussed. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometer was not available for checking final cook temperature of fish baking in the oven in the main kitchen. A food thermometer was located in the cook shack. Thermometer was checked with ice water and observed reading below 20F. Thermometer was calibrated to 32F using ice water method. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed. 
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-803.11 Soiled, damp wiping cloths were observed on the counter by the sani-bucket in the kitchen. PIC stated they were used earlier and were not yet placed in soiled linen storage. Wiping cloths were removed and taken to proper storage area. 
Soiled linens shall be kept in clean, nonabsorbent receptacles or clean, washable laundry bags. Store soiled wiping cloths in the storage container when no longer needed.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:
3-304.15 Workers were observed not using gloves properly in the main kitchen and the cook shack.
Worker in the main kitchen walked out to the dining area and re-entered the kitchen to return to food prep without a handwash and glove change. The worker was also observed wiping gloved hands on his apron. Worker was advised on proper glove use and washed hands prior to putting on a new pair of gloves to continue with food prep.
--Worker in main kitchen put gloved hands in  oven mitts and returned to service line to assemble orders without changing gloves. Worker was advised the inner surface of oven mitts would not be considered a clean surface. Worker washed hands and changed gloves upon request of inspector.
--Worker in cook shack left to get more fish from the outside walkin cooler. Upon returning, the worker continued with task of breading fish without a handwash and glove change. Worker removed gloves upon request of inspector. Worker was observed blowing into a glove prior to putting it on and was advised to cease the practice as doing such may result in saliva and bacteria contaminating the gloves. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sanitizer solution was not available for wiping surfaces in cook shack. Maintain sanitizer solution for wiping surfaces during all hours of operation in both the main kitchen and the cook shack.
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Basin designated for handwashing at cook shack was observed to be heavily soiled with buildup from general use. Clean the designated handsink and related fixtures prior to events and as needed during use. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean
